q: Which agency is now the sole regulator of housing and land use development, encouraging private low-cost housing through simpler rules and decentralized approvals?
n: The DHSUD (RA 11201, 2019) is now the sole regulatory body for housing and land use development. It absorbed the HLURB's planning and regulatory functions and the HUDCC's policy role. Source: RA 11201 (DHSUD Act).

q: Which key shelter agency focuses on the production side of housing?
n: The National Housing Authority (NHA) is the key shelter agency on the production side, directly developing and building housing. Source: PD 757 (NHA Charter); RA 11201.

q: Which housing fund agency is known locally as the Pag-IBIG Fund?
n: The Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF) is known as the Pag-IBIG Fund. Source: RA 9679 (HDMF Law of 2009).

q: Where are the highest-level policy statements on environmental protection?
n: The highest-level policy on environmental protection is the 1987 Constitution. Article II, Sec. 16 guarantees the right to a balanced and healthful ecology. Source: 1987 Philippine Constitution, Art. II Sec. 16.

q: Which law protects selected areas under a local Protected Area Management Board chaired by the DENR?
n: The NIPAS Act (RA 7586, amended by the E-NIPAS Act RA 11038) protects declared areas, each managed by a Protected Area Management Board chaired by the DENR regional executive director. Source: RA 7586 and RA 11038.

q: What plan addresses a community's immediate problems in the short term?
n: An action-oriented plan targets a community's immediate problems over a short period. A comprehensive plan or CLUP is long-range. Source: Branch, Comprehensive City Planning; DHSUD CLUP Guidebook.

q: What clearance is issued to a project allowed under the zoning ordinance and other land use rules?
n: A locational clearance, issued by the zoning administrator, certifies that a project conforms to the zoning ordinance and land use rules. A variance is relief from the ordinance. Source: HLURB/DHSUD Model Zoning Ordinance.

q: Which DENR document certifies that, after EIA review, a project will not cause significant negative environmental impact?
n: The Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC), issued by DENR-EMB after EIA review, certifies the project will not cause significant negative environmental impact. Source: PD 1586; DAO 2003-30.

q: Which law, as amended, requires subdivision developers to set aside part of the project area or cost for socialized housing?
n: RA 7279 (UDHA), as amended by RA 10884, requires developers to provide socialized housing equal to 15% of subdivision project area or cost (5% for condominiums). Source: RA 7279 Sec. 18 as amended by RA 10884.

q: Which code requires every LGU to prepare a comprehensive land use plan and enact it through a zoning ordinance?
n: The Local Government Code (RA 7160) requires every LGU to prepare a comprehensive land use plan enacted through a zoning ordinance. Source: RA 7160, Sec. 20 and Sec. 447/458.

q: What is an encumbrance limiting the use of land, usually for mutual protection?
n: A restriction (deed restriction) is an encumbrance limiting how land may be used, usually imposed for the mutual protection of lot owners. Source: Black's Law Dictionary; DHSUD subdivision rules.

q: What is left of a lot after deducting the required open spaces?
n: The buildable area is what remains of a lot after deducting the required open spaces (setbacks and yards). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII.

q: Which tool controls how raw land is subdivided and marketed for housing?
n: Subdivision regulations control how raw land is divided and marketed for housing, setting standards for lots, roads, open space and utilities. Source: PD 957 & IRR; BP 220 & IRR.

q: Who develops land and builds houses on it?
n: Developers acquire land, improve it and build houses on it for sale. Source: PD 957, Sec. 2 (definitions).

q: A land development decision is also what kind of decision?
n: A land development decision commits land to a particular use, so it is also a land use decision. Source: Chapin & Kaiser, Urban Land Use Planning.

q: What type of survey is used to locate utilities and roads?
n: A topographic survey maps ground relief and features such as roads, utilities and structures. Source: Davis & Foote, Surveying: Theory and Practice; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What type of surveying involves the surveyor plotting points first and then placing the monuments in their proper locations afterward?
n: Setting out (staking out) first plots or computes points, then places monuments or stakes at those positions on the ground. Source: Davis & Foote, Surveying: Theory and Practice.

q: What type of surveying is used to locate utilities, roads, and other features on the ground?
n: A topographic survey locates utilities, roads and other natural and man-made features on the ground. Source: Davis & Foote, Surveying: Theory and Practice.

q: Where is a lot's technical description found?
n: A lot's technical description (bearings, distances, area) is written on its Transfer Certificate of Title. Source: PD 1529 (Property Registration Decree).

q: OCT stands for:
n: OCT means Original Certificate of Title, the first title issued for land after original registration. Later transfers get TCTs. Source: PD 1529, Sec. 39–43.

q: Amap that shows the spatial allocation of built-up areas categorized as residential, commercial, institutional, parks and open spaces, industrial, and others.
n: An urban land use map shows how built-up areas are allocated among residential, commercial, institutional, industrial, parks and open space and other uses. Source: DHSUD CLUP Guidebook.

q: What written instrument transfers property from one person to another?
n: A deed is a written instrument that transfers property or an interest in it from one person to another, such as a deed of sale or donation. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines; Black's Law Dictionary.

q: What is the gradual paying off of a debt through periodic payments?
n: Amortization is paying off a debt gradually through periodic payments, each covering interest and part of the principal. Source: Brigham & Houston, Fundamentals of Financial Management.

q: Which government arm develops and carries out low-cost housing in the Philippines?
n: The National Housing Authority is the government arm that develops and carries out low-cost housing in the Philippines. Source: PD 757 (NHA Charter).

q: What is a city governed by its own charter rather than general law?
n: A chartered city is created and governed by its own legislative charter rather than by general law alone. Source: RA 7160, Book III; Philippine city charters.

q: What deposit, sometimes called subscription money, shows a buyer is serious?
n: Earnest money (subscription money) is a deposit showing the buyer's serious intent. It forms part of the purchase price. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1482.

q: What is dividing land into lots that are easier to sell or develop, usually through a plat?
n: Subdivision is dividing land into lots for easier sale or development, typically shown on a plat. Source: PD 957, Sec. 2.

q: What does the Local Government Code require in planning?
o: LGUs must prepare comprehensive land use plans and enact them through zoning ordinances
n: The Local Government Code requires LGUs to prepare comprehensive land use plans and enact them through zoning ordinances. Source: RA 7160, Sec. 20.

q: What is a plat for in subdivision development?
o: Defining property boundaries and the legal description of land
n: A plat (subdivision plan) maps the lots, blocks and roads, defining property boundaries and the legal description of the land. Source: PD 957 IRR; PD 1529.
